[b][color=white]Tesla Invests in Bitcoin[/color][/b]
On February 8, news broke that Tesla had invested over $1.5 billion in Bitcoin. The company's CEO, Elon Musk, had been promoting Bitcoin and Dogecoin on his personal Twitter account for some time, and this move should come as no surprise if you take that into account. According to Tesla, the investment was done as part of an aim to "diversify and maximize returns on our cash" and was revealed in their annual report. This is in reference to cash that is not a necessity to "maintain [an] adequate operating liquidity." The company hopes to start accepting orders that use Bitcoin as a payment method in the near future as well. Following the news, the price for Bitcoin jumped by over $4,000 within an hour. Throughout 2020, many companies invested in cryptocurrencies as an alternative way to generate an income during the coronavirus pandemic. Tesla joined them with one of the largest investments in crypto made by a company, paving the way for other large corporations to do so. [i][size=x-small][url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/tesla-buys-1-5-billion-in-bitcoin-11612791688]>>Source[/url][/size][/i]

[b][color=white]Twitter CEO Announces Bitcoin Development Fund[/color][/b]
Jack Dorsey and Jay-Z have joined together to launch an endowment that is intended to fund Bitcoin Development. The fund was launched with 500 Bitcoin, worth roughly $24 million dollars at the time of writing. Named ₿trust, it will "initially [be] focused on team in Africa and India" and shall be "set up as a blind irrevocable trust." This means that Dorsey would not be able to revoke or change ₿trust at any point in time, ensuring its security. The fund has already received attention from the likes of Binance CEO Changpeng Zhao, who expressed an interest in making a donation once it is up and running. The news came after reports that Twitter is considering investing in Bitcoin. [i][size=x-small][url=https://edition.cnn.com/2021/02/12/business/bitcoin-jack-dorsey-jay-z/index.html]>>Source[/url][/size][/i]
